about: ZoomFrames on the new machine, 2026-10-17 (ET), seed 1, Apple M3 Pro (Metal-3, unified memory), macOS 15.8, headless Chrome 155.0.8059.85 at window 1600x1143 (a 1600x1000 view), tree 5949021 for the page (the later sodden fix, 1cc7cb5, touches no page code), the default load (warm of one sim day, speed 600), ?bench=zoom,orbit,turn,pan on one load, one 12 s run per bench after the warm. The figures at the top level are on AC power (pmset: 'AC Power', 44% charging, lowpowermode 0). The first run of all of this, on battery at 20% with Low Power Mode on, is kept under onBattery. Baseline: bench-sim-worker.json (AMD Radeon Pro 5500M). A scratch rAF logger was injected at load for the midnight and warm figures (not committed).
changes: none: a measurement. The same session found and fixed one sim crash (the sodden condition, commit 1cc7cb5), unrelated to the page.

firstViewAndWarm.note: page time from navigation start on the default load (with the rAF logger); firstViewMs is the page's own revealMs
firstViewAndWarm.before: AMD Mac (napkin, 2026-10-17): body.ready 62 s, the warm 46 s more.

midnight.note: rAF gaps from the page thread around the warm's last tick (the sim reaching t 86400: the first midnight and the daily smalls step)
midnight.before: bench-r9e.json: longest 50 ms on the AMD Mac (2,850 ms before the sliced step)

spinUpStall.note: the first 12.5 s after the sim exists, before the first view: 22 rAF gaps over 100 ms, longest 567 ms, about one every 0.5 s (350, 233, 550, 150, 317, 533, 117, 167, 350, 450, 283, 517, 350, 483, 300, 533, 317, 533, 350, 567, 283, 550 ms); none in the last 12 s before the warm's end. It is the first tick's spin-up, which sends each lumped split as one dispatch (smalls.ts spin and day with bins Infinity). No hang, no page error. The handoff's remedy (SPLIT_BINS slices, unpaced) was not applied: it asked for it only if the page or GPU hangs.

dailyStep.note: scripts/_r9f2.ts (scratch, not committed): seed 1, random brain, on AC power, ticks run as the page's worker runs them (sim.ts tickPause awaiting the GPU idle after each upload, slice and law), 4 sim days; the time of each stretch of recording plus GPU between two yields, by the tick's class. Budget 50 ms.
dailyStep.over50: t 25,980 (7.2 h in), 94.1 ms and 39.6 ms: the first landing after the first fire, the bed kernel's first compile (fire-constants gap)
dailyStep.onBattery: the same run on battery in Low Power Mode: day max 48.5 ms, p99 21.4, one other chunk of 107.6 ms at the same tick
dailyStep.unpaced: the same day ticks with no yields (bun, begin in one piece), on battery: the whole tick 1,435 to 1,901 ms at days 1 to 10, rising slowly; one 13.0 s tick at t 25,921 (the bed kernel compiling cold, 24 to 38 s on the AMD Mac).
dailyStep.before: bench-r9.json dailyStep: the day 51 to 71 ms on AMD after, 71 to 89 ms before

gpuMemory.note: scripts/_r9f.ts (scratch): seed 1, random brain, device.createBuffer and destroy wrapped, every buffer counted as made and destroyed (textures not counted), MiB as the plan counts them, at each sim day's midnight; the budget is 1.5 GB [design]
gpuMemory.note2: within 1.5 GiB (1,536 MiB) by 39 MiB at day 10 and growing in steps (day 4, 5, 9: lumped tables and the fish rooms taking their next size); the plan's own run at bf7b503 was 1,473.4 live and 1,484.3 most over three days. Over 1.5 decimal GB (1,430 MiB) from day 5.

onBattery.note: the first run, before the Mac was plugged in: battery at 20%, Low Power Mode on
onBattery.reading: zoom held 60 fps, then orbit, turn and pan sat at exactly 30 fps (every page frame two vsyncs) with worker GPU time at its usual 6.6 to 7.9 ms; plugged in the same load holds 60 fps in all four. Benches on battery in Low Power Mode are not a reading of the renderer.

verdict: R9 on this machine, plugged in: all four benches hold 60 fps (59.9, 60, 59.9, 60; baseline zoom 54.8). Worker GPU mean 5.02, 5.2, 4.72, 5.93 ms against 7.8, 6.59, 7.92, 6.69; p95 9.05, 7.28, 7.56, 9.29 against 13.57, 8.67, 10.83, 12.5; frames over 16.7 ms 5, 1, 1, 0 against 8, 0, 1, 0. Not clean: one worker frame of 33.93 ms in orbit (baseline max 15.55) and 24.14 ms in zoom (21.21), and one 33.3 ms page frame in each of zoom and turn; no long tasks. Midnight: no rAF gap over 40 ms from 10 s before the warm's last tick to 20 s after (longest 33.4 ms), so the 2.85 s stall stays gone. Daily GPU step: the longest stretch between yields is 48.6 ms, under the 50 ms budget (the AMD Mac needed 51 to 71). First view 21 s, warm of one day 24.5 s (the AMD Mac: 62 s and 46 s more). Memory: 1,497 MiB at the most over 10 days, inside 1.5 GiB by 39 MiB and growing in steps. Open: 22 page rAF gaps of 117 to 567 ms in the load's first 12.5 s (the spin-up's unpaced whole-split dispatches, before the first view); the bed kernel's first compile (94 ms chunk at the first fire). Per-pass timestamps from Metal are not trustworthy (a pass's time was negative in some slowest frames), so the passes' split is not recorded; the frame's first-to-last span (gpuMs) is. After the timestamp fix a second run held 60 fps in all four benches with no page frame over 16.8 ms in 2,884, worker GPU mean 5.80, 5.16, 4.96 and 5.49 ms; the worker's maxima (15 to 33 ms) are Metal timestamp noise, not frames the page dropped (napkin, renderer rule).

afterTimestampFix.note: a second AC-power run of the same load after webgpu.js left backwards and over-a-second timestamp pairs out of a frame's span (Metal gave pairs hours apart, which read as frames of 30 ms or more beside passes of 8). Not the same frames as afterWarm, so its worker maxima differ.
afterTimestampFix.reading: page frames: 2,884 across the four benches and not one over 16.8 ms (afterWarm had one 33.3 ms frame in each of zoom and turn). Worker maxima of 15 to 33 ms remain in frames whose valid passes sum to under 11 ms, with the page showing no hitch: Metal's pass timestamps are noise at the maxima, so judge the means, p95 and the page's dt.
